claims.text: IMF WEO April 2025 database (vintage April 2025) lists Maldives nominal GDP (NGDPD, current prices, USD) at $7.08bn for 2024 est. and $7.52bn for 2025 projection; World Bank WDI (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, accessed Sep 2026) lists $6.59bn (2023) and $7.12bn (2024 est.), consistent within revision vintage. Using IMF WEO April 2025 2025 projection $7.52bn as denominator: $12bn = 1.60x GDP (12/7.52), $20bn = 2.66x GDP (20/7.52), $30bn gross = 3.99x GDP (30/7.52). Using World Bank 2024 $7.12bn: $12bn=1.69x, $20bn=2.81x, $30bn=4.21x. Headline 'Double Its GDP' holds for $12-20bn range under either vintage; $30bn gross is ~4x GDP. Ratios must be cited with vintage due to small-economy revisions.

claims.text: Carnegie Endowment 'Mapping the Indian Ocean Region' (Baruah et al., June 15 2023, full PDF pp. 18-24, 42-48) maps UAE as a major extra-regional economic partner with trade/investment ties across multiple Indian Ocean sub-regions (East Africa, Western Indian Ocean islands, South Asia, Southeast Asia) and documents UAE investments in ports/terminals, logistics and shipyards (e.g., DP World operations in Berbera, Sokhna, Karachi; AD Ports). Report does NOT claim 'partner on every coast' as uniform strategic partnership nor 'naval bases on every coast'; it distinguishes commercial port/logistics footprint from naval capability, noting Saudi/UAE naval ambitions are aspirational and concentrated in Red Sea/Gulf of Aden. UAE Ministry of Economy outward FDI data (2022-2023) shows MENA/South Asia as top destinations but Indian Ocean littoral share is fragmented by country, not a single Indian Ocean strategy envelope. Lowy/IISS trackers confirm UAE port footprint is significant but selective, not littoral-wide.

claims.text: IMF Maldives 2024 Article IV Staff Report (Country Report No. 24/106, May 2024, DSA Annex pp. 28-38) assesses Maldives at 'high risk of external and overall debt distress' with public debt 122.8% GDP in 2023, breach of all external DSA thresholds under baseline, and no space to absorb shocks; debt deemed unsustainable without adjustment. World Bank Maldives Development Update June 2026 (full PDF Tables 1-3, pp. 12-18, 24-26) updates: public and publicly guaranteed debt 129.7% GDP in 2025, projected >140% medium term; external debt service $630m (2025) spiking to $1.7bn (2026), remaining ~$1.0bn after $500m Sukuk + $400m RBI swap settled April 2026; current account deficit 7.5% GDP (2025) projected to widen to 20.6% GDP (2026) on tourism disruption/fuel prices; fiscal deficit 4.3% GDP (2025) widening to 10.9% GDP (2026). Sovereign-bank nexus: banks' exposure to sovereign rose sharply, constraining private credit (MDU 2026 p.15, Fig. 12).

claims.text: Maldives EPA (now Environmental Regulatory Authority) EIA for Ras Malé / Fushi Dhiggaru Lagoon reclamation (EPA ref: EIA 2023/14, approved Dec 2023, 312pp) discloses 1,150ha dredge-and-fill, borrow areas in lagoon, sediment plume modeling to 5km, and coral relocation plan; approval conditioned on turbidity curtains and real-time monitoring. EPA Dredging Suspension Order No. 438-ECAS/2024/12 (May 9 2024) ordered halt of all dredging/reclamation until June 10 2024 during national coral bleaching alert (NOAA Alert Level 1), citing SST anomaly +0.9C; order lifted June 11 with enhanced monitoring. HRW 'We Still Haven't Recovered' (Oct 2023, methodology pp. 12-15, 78 interviews, satellite analysis) documents prior reclamations (Kulhudhuffushi 70% mangrove loss, reef burial) and finds EIAs often post-contract, EPA lacks independence (under Ministry) and has 6 staff for 200+ active EIAs with no public compliance database. Pulitzer Center sediment study (2024) measured plumes 3-8km from dredge sites, exceeding EIA predictions. Eagle Hills claim of 'no further dredging' refers to 500ha parcel already reclaimed, not lagoon-wide works.
